text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Traffic minister awards telecom licences to Enertel (utilities) and Telfort (Dutch Rail and British Telecom). (p1)
- Economic affairs ministry rejects Samsung's letter of intent on takeover of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p1)
- Philips entertainment unit PolyGram's full year net profit may be lower than last year's. (p1)
- Business software co. Baan books 80 pct higher Q3 net (p3)
- Realty investor Uni-Invest buys Dutch portfolio of Derksen family and Homburg Dover Group. (p3)
- Joint profit of major Dutch companies (excluding banks and insurers) rose by 18 pct to Dfl 43 billion last year. (p3)
- Chemicals group DSM tightens bond with U.S. pharma giant Bristol-Myers Squibb. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- U.S. bus company Vancom draws 50 pct more passengers in South Limburg province than last year. (p1)
- Smit Internationale's supply-ships unit Smit Lloyd demands 18 pct "voluntary" pay cut. (p2)
- Dutch transporters association KNV suspects oil companies of cartel. (p37)
- Large banks force Dutch PTT (KPN) to alter the contracting
out of a Dfl 2.25 billion loan. (p37)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Commercial sports-only TV channel Sport7 seeks to remedy poor performance. (p1)
- Philips and four partners say they will launch re-writable CD's next year. (p35)
- Papermaker KNP BT unit BT Office Products books Q3 net of $2.7 million versus $2.1 million in same period of 1995. (p35)
- Consumer organisation says insurers' saving schemes are often misleading. (p39)
TROUW
- PM Wim Kok wants to make building of second national airport an issue for forming the next Dutch cabinet. (p1) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Two-thirds of Dutch consumers do not want "electronic purse" -- research poll. (p10)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM and partner Northwest raise prices due to higher kerosene costs. (p11)
